section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch13 — Assessment & CCE
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher gives a short quiz every week purely to identify which concepts need re-teaching, without recording marks on the report card. This is an example of:
explanation: Formative assessment happens during learning to give feedback and guide instruction. Summative assessment evaluates learning at the end of a unit for grading.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch13 — Assessment & CCE
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Under Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE), a pupil's participation in sports, art and value-based activities is assessed under the:
explanation: CCE assesses two domains — scholastic (academic subjects) and co-scholastic (life skills, attitudes, values, sports, art) — reflecting its 'comprehensive' aspect.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch12 — Individual Differences
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: The principle that no two children — even identical twins raised together — develop at exactly the same rate is the principle of:
explanation: While the general sequence of development is universal, the rate and degree differ from child to child — the principle underlying differentiated instruction.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch12 — Individual Differences
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher seats a child with mild hearing loss in the front row, uses visual cues alongside speech, and pairs them with a peer buddy — while keeping the child in the same regular classroom. This approach reflects:

options.option_text: Integration only, with no curriculum accommodation

explanation: Inclusive education keeps children with disabilities in the mainstream classroom with reasonable accommodations tailored to need — distinct from segregation or mere physical integration without support.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch12 — Individual Differences
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A pupil who can generate many different, unusual uses for a simple brick is displaying strong:
explanation: Divergent thinking generates multiple original solutions/uses — the hallmark of creativity (J.P. Guilford). Convergent thinking narrows toward one correct answer.
